The 19th-century social reform movement in western India produced radical critiques of patriarchal gender norms. In 1882, Tarabai Shinde published 'Stri Purush Tulana' (A Comparison between Women and Men), which is considered one of the earliest indigenous feminist texts in modern Indian history.
